name: Agent-First Terminal
synopsis: Let your AI agent work in a real terminal you can watch — and take the keyboard back whenever you want, from your phone if you are not at the machine.
intent: Expose Rust APIs for opening, tracking, resizing, signaling, and streaming one or many trusted local terminal sessions
Coordinate multiple human and automated input actors with shared or exclusive TTL leases and immediate human preemption
Take secret input in a session without publishing anything derived from its bytes, suspending every non-human actor until the person ends the window
Expose the same multi-session runtime through a loopback-only bearer-protected OpenAPI 3.2 HTTP API for external controllers
Let the afterminal CLI open a trusted local DOM-rendered terminal window over a new runtime or attach midway to sessions owned by an already-running API server
Keep the PTY runtime independent of any UI host or application-specific task model, with AFUI hosting only the CLI's window
Provide bounded scrollback subscriptions without coupling terminal output to any UI data model
mutations: First release: a multi-session PTY runtime an agent can drive and a person can watch, with raw fan-out, structured VT screen snapshots, a multiplexed event stream, resize, foreground process-group signals and typed lifecycle operations
Coordinate several actors on one terminal through shared and exclusive input leases with TTL deadlines, where a person needs no lease and typing immediately revokes an automated exclusive one

Take secret input without publishing anything derived from it — no raw output, nothing retained for replay, no screen content, and no event carrying the size of what was typed — refusing every non-human actor until a person ends it

Deliver a trusted DOM-rendered terminal page as a local window, an AFUI-owned LAN link, or a registered AFUI session, and let a command run inside a remotely delivered session publish into the same registry rather than opening a window nobody is at
Expose the same runtime to programs over a loopback-only bearer-protected HTTP API with a committed, drift-tested OpenAPI 3.2 contract and an SSE stream that resumes from Last-Event-ID
Keep the core library free of an async runtime, an HTTP dependency and any UI host, so depending on this crate needs no feature and the CLI's api feature is opt-in
Send a special key only after the text typed before it, so Return no longer reaches the PTY ahead of its own line and Backspace no longer arrives before the character it deletes
Stop swallowing the first keystroke after an input method commits, which on a Chinese keyboard was the space between two words
Replace only the screen rows that changed and leave a selection alone when a click ends a drag, so output can be selected and copied while the screen refreshes
Put the composition field on the cursor and show the text being composed there, so a half-typed word appears where it is typed and an input method's candidate window follows the cursor
Give the terminal its height back on a phone held sideways, where every responsive rule keyed off width and left under one row once a keyboard opened
Publish through Homebrew and Scoop alongside crates.io and GitHub Releases

bonds.reason: CLI discovery, output routing, redaction, and protocol events follow Agent-First Data conventions
The `api` feature builds the afterminal CLI window on Agent-First UI, which owns the browser process, its disposable profile, the UI credential, and the security headers
